topics.topic: SpooledFile identity facts
questions: Is a SpooledFile identified solely by run/node/map/attempt/port/list position, or by all M22 facts including content and class?
Is a SpooledFile's identity its producing position alone, or all M22 facts including its content and class?

judgement.why: This is the same SpooledFile identity question as P4, and the multipart-only change altered none of the relevant text.

quotes:
A SpooledFile is named by
its producing position alone (SpooledFileKey); a file already at that position
that no SpooledFile record names — left by a change that failed — is replaced,
and one a record names is never overwritten: that call is `internal_error`.
precedent.why: State 5 explicitly defines the producer-position SpooledFileKey as the lookup identity.

topics.topic: authored trial file bytes representation and distinction from file facts
questions: What representation supplies bytes for authored file inputs and expected file outputs, and how is it distinguished from the digest/size/media-type facts used only for checks?
What exactly must a caller supply for a file input or expected file output of an authored trial case: bytes, file facts, or both, and how are those bytes represented at the MCP boundary?

quotes:
`capability:functions.add_trial_case` takes a contract
   version and the case's input values, expected outputs optional. It checks
   each value against its port with `capability:canonical_values.fit_port_value`,
   ports in name order — presence, carriage, schema,
   size — and the size ceilings `stored_value_bytes_max` and
   `trial_fixture_bytes_max`, naming the first failure (A04 rule 1).
judgement.why: The post-closure change concerns multipart approval framing and did not touch or make the authored-trial payload representation matter.

topics.topic: masked failure_detail length measurement
questions: Is the disclosed length measured in Unicode code points, UTF-8 bytes before truncation, or UTF-8 bytes after replacement and truncation?
Is the reported length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, characters after replacement and truncation, or the original untruncated detail?

judgement.why: This is the same masked failure-detail length question as P14, and the multipart-only change altered none of the relevant text.

precedent.topic: Measurement unit for masked failure-detail length
quotes: handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
precedent.why: The later notes explicitly define the disclosed length as the UTF-8 byte length.

topics.topic: oversized value output handling in trials and admission
questions: Who checks `stored_value_bytes_max` for a successful sandbox value output during `try_implementation` or admission, and what TrialExecution outcome is recorded when it is exceeded?
How do `try_implementation` and admission handle an otherwise successful value output whose canonical bytes exceed `stored_value_bytes_max`?

quotes:
outputs validated against the output ports with
`canonical_values.fit_port_value`, the bound passed being the execution's
`output_bytes`; `stored_value_bytes_max` and the spool ceilings are not the
sandbox's — `runs` and `store` apply them after the execution has otherwise
succeeded (A15 rules 3 and 4).
judgement.why: The post-closure change concerns multipart approval framing and did not touch or make trial-output size handling matter.

topics.topic: sandbox failure detail handling in trial and admission executions
questions: What happens to a sandbox failure detail during a trial or admission execution?
Is a trial or admission execution's sandbox failure detail stored and returned, discarded, or represented by a new TrialExecution field?

quotes:
With the output count taken through `canonical_values.canonical_bytes`, exactly
one outcome of `timeout`, `resource_exhausted`, `sandbox_violation`, `crashed`,
`contract_violation`, `succeeded`; on success the outputs by port; resources
used; a bounded `failure_detail` otherwise.
judgement.why: The post-closure change concerns multipart approval framing and did not touch or make trial failure-detail retention matter.

topics.topic: sandbox startup probe definition and verified guarantees
questions: What code, inputs, bounds and expected observations constitute the probe, and which sandbox guarantees must it exercise before startup succeeds?
What exact probe is run, and which isolation properties must it actively verify before startup succeeds?

quotes: Check at start that bubblewrap is present and one probe execution succeeds.
judgement.why: The post-closure change concerns multipart approval framing and did not touch or make the sandbox probe definition matter.

topics.topic: spool-ceiling refusal cleanup and state semantics
questions: If removing files already spooled by the same attempt fails while handling a ceiling refusal, which result is returned and what state may remain?
Is a spool-ceiling result a refusal governed by the no-change convention, or a special failure allowed to delete files published by earlier `spool_file` calls for the attempt?

judgement.why: This is the same spool-ceiling cleanup and residual-state question as P5, and the multipart-only change altered none of the relevant text.

precedent.topic: Atomicity, cleanup, return value, and residual state when spool_file refuses at the spool ceiling
quotes: spool_file: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise RefusedError when the size of content exceeds the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SPOOL_FILE_BYTES_MAX constant, or when the run's spool, counted as the bytes of the files already in it, less a file no SpooledFile record names at this file's position, plus content, would exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SPOOL_RUN_BYTES_MAX constant; on that refusal it removes this file and every file already spooled under the same run_id, producer_node_id, map_index and attempt_number, so nothing of that attempt's files is kept, while files of earlier attempts stay. The attempt_number of the key is the element's next number as the caller read it; spool_file does not assign one.

spool_file: [VALIDATION_ERROR] When removing this attempt's files on a ceiling refusal fails, MUST raise StoreInternalError instead of RefusedError, so a caller never reads a refusal as "nothing of the attempt is kept" while files of it remain; the files left stay unnamed in the run's spool, counted toward the spool ceiling, until remove_run_spool or a later write to their position.

spool_file: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns FileFacts with the hexadecimal SHA-256 content_digest, size_bytes and the given media_type; it writes no SpooledFile record, which the caller's later record_change writes.
precedent.why: State 6 explicitly permits a ceiling refusal to remove files from earlier spool_file calls for the same attempt, converts cleanup failure to StoreInternalError with unnamed residual files, and defines the successful return value.

topics.topic: startup manifest and capability validation scope
questions: Which A08 rule 5 checks are performed at startup when `check_installed_instances` has no operation name, binding ports or proposal with which to perform the operation-specific checks?
Which exact manifest checks and which capability entries are examined for each credentialed service during startup?

judgement.why: This is the same startup manifest-check scope question as P12, and the multipart-only change altered none of the relevant text.

precedent.topic: Exact startup manifest checks performed by check_installed_instances
quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
precedent.why: The later notes limit startup validation to credential-bearing services, ordered by service_id, and to top-level service-record checks plus the selected instance's credential-header collision.

topics.topic: EffectAttempt concluded_at semantics after unknown resolution
questions: When an `unknown` attempt is resolved, does `concluded_at` retain the time the transport outcome became unknown, change to the resolution time, or is a separate resolution timestamp required?

topics.topic: canonical tie-breaking for edges and constants
questions: How are ties broken when distinct guarded edges have the same A05 endpoint-order key, or distinct constants target the same port, so reversing them cannot change `flow_version_id`?

topics.topic: canonical_bytes input representation and duplicate-key preservation
questions: Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text, a duplicate-preserving parsed representation, or an ordinary parsed value that can no longer reveal duplicate keys?

topics.topic: credential-byte collisions in approval preview content
questions: What happens if an input value, URL component, required-header value or multipart content happens to contain the credential bytes verbatim?

topics.topic: duplicate selected instance names in a manifest
questions: What happens when a service manifest contains two instance entries with the selected instance name?

topics.topic: effect-class mismatch in send_prepared_request
questions: What happens if the separately supplied effect class differs from the class of the ManifestOperation used to prepare the request?

topics.topic: handling incompatible or corrupt existing stores
questions: What must `open_store` do with an existing incompatible or corrupt store, especially when A20 permits a new release to execute records created by an earlier release?

topics.topic: meaning of an earlier implementation for rollback
questions: What makes an implementation “earlier”: creation before the currently active implementation, an earlier activation in the slot's history, or merely any admitted implementation that is not current?

topics.topic: monotonic_deadline return object and expiration semantics
questions: What exact object or operations are returned, and precisely when is the deadline considered passed?

topics.topic: open_store partial-initialization failure and rollback semantics
questions: What does `open_store` return if initialization fails after creating part of the store, and must those created artifacts be rolled back or left for the next start?

topics.topic: open_store privacy and symbolic-link checks
questions: Exactly what makes the data directory private, and which path components and existing descendants must be checked for symbolic links at open time?

topics.topic: persistence and return location of operation failure detail codes
questions: Where is the closed machine detail code stored and returned when a NodeExecution also has diagnostic body text?

topics.topic: record position assignment order within store changes
questions: In what exact order does each named store change assign positions to its newly created records?

topics.topic: required coverage and semantics of TrialCase expected outputs
questions: When expected outputs are present, must they cover exactly all contract output ports, or may they cover only a subset, and if partial expectations are allowed what makes the unlisted outputs pass?

topics.topic: service base URL validity, joining, wire form, and digest representation
questions: Are base URLs containing user information, a path prefix, query, fragment, percent-encoded authority text or noncanonical host forms valid, and exactly how are they joined and represented on the wire and in `request_digest`?

topics.topic: timestamp sampling and ordering within one store change
questions: When one store change writes several timestamped records or fields, are their timestamps identical or sampled separately, and in what order?

topics.topic: whether the response-token prohibition includes continuation tokens
questions: Does the prohibition cover only owner and agent authentication tokens, or continuation tokens as well?
